standard_prerequisites.name: An element that is neither irreducible nor a unit factors into two proper factors
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the next element of the descending divisibility sequence from a failure of irreducibility.

standard_prerequisites.name: The ascending chain condition for principal ideals
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Contradicted at the end of the counted proof (lines 29624-29626)
standard_prerequisites.use: Forbids the strictly increasing chain of principal ideals constructed from the descending sequence.

core_obligations: Argue by contradiction: start from a nonzero nonunit x that has no factorization into irreducibles and write x = yz with neither factor irreducible or a unit (proof lines 29613-29616).
Observe that at least one of the two factors still has no factorization into irreducibles, and take it as the next element of the sequence; iterate (proof lines 29617-29621).
Obtain a sequence in which each term divides the previous one with nonunit quotient, hence a strictly increasing chain of principal ideals, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 29622-29626).
proof_roadmap: Build a descending divisibility sequence out of a hypothetical element without a factorization (proof lines 29612-29621).
Turn the sequence into a strictly increasing chain of principal ideals and contradict the chain condition (proof lines 29622-29627).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a domain, the ascending chain condition for principal ideals implies that every nonzero nonunit admits a factorization into irreducibles (statement lines 29599-29610). The proof does not measure the number of factors or invoke a height function: assuming an element with no such factorization, it splits that element into two proper factors, notes that at least one factor again has no factorization, and iterates, obtaining a sequence in which each term divides the previous one with nonunit quotient; the corresponding principal ideals then increase strictly, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 29612-29627). The pigeonhole step choosing the bad factor is what drives the construction, and the author spells it out. H2.
